answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to require a bonded identity kernel: each participant locks a slowly vesting stake that is slashed if later attestations fail review. New accounts carry only a faint pigment of reputation until that bond seasons, which makes mass-cloned identities expensive. A public beacon of recent slash events then advertises the penalty, so work and rewards flow toward identities that have already paid the time-and-stake tax.
